open_release.rationale: The paper frames synthetic EHR as a way around restricted access to patient data, but never states the output is meant to be released.

quotes.text: due to privacy constraints, limited access to EHR becomes a bottleneck for deep learning research. To mitigate these concerns, generative adversarial networks (GANs) have been successfully used for generating EHR data.

pipeline_testing.rationale: No testing or format-conformance use appears in the paper or README.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The paper evaluates the synthetic data with prediction tasks on health events.

quotes.text: Furthermore, we design multiple statistical metrics and prediction tasks to evaluate the generated data.

statistical_replication.rationale: The paper evaluates fidelity with statistical metrics and claims realistic synthetic EHR.

quotes.text: Experimental results demonstrate the quality of the synthetic data and the effectiveness of MTGAN in generating realistic sequential EHR data, especially for uncommon diseases.

causal_inference.rationale: No causal structure or intervention framing in the sources.

education.rationale: No teaching or tutorial framing; the README only gives preprocessing, training and generation commands.

benchmarking.rationale: MTGAN is compared against other GANs in its own experiments but is not offered as a baseline or benchmark dataset.

imbalance_correction.rationale: A central goal is better generation of uncommon (minority) diseases in imbalanced EHR data.

quotes.text: we propose a Multi-label Time-series GAN (MTGAN) to generate EHR and simultaneously improve the quality of uncommon disease generation.
